name: Game art and interactive assets
one_line: Engine-facing game assets whose authored source, review proof, exported/imported copy, and integration versions form one production family: sprites, textures, models, rigs, animation clips, UI atlases, VFX, and sometimes authored audio. The discriminator is production-to-engine handoff evidence, not an extension or stylised appearance. Absorbs legacy soft.game-development-asset.
design_cite: Design and creative formats such as PSD, AI, SVG, Figma exports, CAD files, and 3D files should at minimum yield filename, format, dimensions or canvas properties, embedded metadata, layers or artboards where accessible, linked asset names, and preview text; unsupported proprietary formats should be recorded as indexed-but-unreadable rather than silently treated as empty.

deterministic: An asset family has authored source plus export/import settings or manifest and an engine-side asset, prefab, scene, or UI reference sharing a stem, GUID, asset ID, or explicit path reference.
A 2D packet has layered/vector source, sprite-sheet or atlas output, pivot/trim/scale metadata, and a matching engine import configuration or prefab/UI reference.
A 3D packet has model/scene source, material or texture dependencies, rig or animation clips, and an export or engine-import record; a lone model is insufficient.
A review packet has rendered preview, turntable, gameplay capture, annotated image, or change list naming an asset/variant and linking to source or export.
An integration packet has an engine asset, prefab/scene reference, import settings, generated atlas, build report, or manifest recording imported copy and version/dependency relationship.

A version family links source, review, export, or integration artifacts with explicit revision sequence, changelog/build identifier, or hash relationship; a filename token alone is not current-version proof.
needs_llm: whether stylised media is authored game content, concept/reference, marketing render, or ordinary creative work without engine linkage
whether an engine project is the consuming game, tutorial/sample, marketplace package, or unrelated repository
whether source and imported files are the same asset after re-export, atlas packing, compression, or generated naming
whether a review capture is asset integration evidence, bug report, portfolio reel, or detached screenshot
whether a package is licensed third-party content, internal original, or derivative
whether sound belongs to game-asset production or a music/audio session
whether final/approved/master/v12 records lifecycle state or stale copied labelling
never_alone: game, asset, sprite, character, level, texture, atlas, rig, VFX, UI, export, import, prefab, final, approved, or build in a filename alone
a lone engine directory, executable, cache, Library/Intermediate folder, or package lock file
a screenshot, gameplay video, GIF, or render without source/export/import evidence
a bare version token, date, GUID, or checksum without linked lifecycle context
vendor, studio, software, copyright, or author metadata without role-bearing production evidence
a bounded download session of a game, asset pack, tutorial, samples, or installer
dimensions, alpha, UVs, bones, or stylised appearance without engine-consumption evidence

work_types: prefab, scene, UI screen, or asset reference
grouping_reasons: Join source, dependencies, review proof, export, imported copy, and consuming prefab/scene by explicit reference, basename, stable ID, or hash without copying missing facts.
Join a review round's proof, annotations, issue list, source revision, and resulting export/import check; a date is an observation, not automatic approval.
Join platform/engine variants, atlas/compression variants, manifests, and checksums when one handoff is identified; archive paths are not facts.
Join imported asset, prefab/scene reference, import settings, build result, and migration note as one integration change.
Join source and generated copies by hash, explicit lineage, or engine GUID mapping; final does not establish current.
No group for detached concept art, downloaded pack, cache, or lone model with no authored-production and consumption evidence.

template.why: EMPTY BY BINDING CONTRACT: creative declares no legal destination fields, so this template cannot emit project, lifecycle_stage, asset_type, engine_target, or version as folder dimensions. Future licensing should recommend production context, lifecycle stage, then asset type, with engine target only when directly evidenced; do not make time first. The stable unit is source -> review -> export -> import -> integration/build verification. Keep source and engine-side copy co-retrievable through structural links and preserve references when moving could break an engine path or GUID. This is a recommendation, not a path or activation fact.

observations: layer groups separate body, costume, shadow, effects; atlas manifest names pivot policy
must_not_conclude: engine, game, character, authorship, export existence, or folder path from filename

observations: packed image has trimmed sprites and transparent padding; sidecar maps frame rectangles and pivots
must_not_conclude: engine import, current version, or hero fact from filename

observations: structured data maps atlas regions to animation names and import settings; references a prefab ID
must_not_conclude: JSON is necessarily source code or import succeeded

observations: container has mesh, skeleton, named animation takes; import record maps it to a rig
must_not_conclude: authorship, license, or game membership from extension

observations: engine binary pairs with source model and records skeleton/material/import properties in metadata; prefab consumes animation
must_not_conclude: unreadable body, approval, build success, or folder path

observations: screen capture shows effect in engine scene with issue marker; notes link timing change to export revision
must_not_conclude: approval, finality, engine identity, or source footage distinction from filename

observations: annotated proof lists colour, timing, overdraw, integration issues and retest build
must_not_conclude: all issues fixed, client approval, or rights

observations: rows map IDs to imported paths, hashes, package version, and build status; manifest contains no assets
must_not_conclude: paths still exist, legal acceptance, or engine fact without packet

observations: manifest contains prefabs, textures, materials and vendor-like names; no local source/review/consumer
must_not_conclude: local authorship, production stage, safe extraction, or internal family

observations: single illustration has no export, engine reference, review note, or project metadata
must_not_conclude: game production, artist, date, or character role from visual content

observations: engine binary sits in repository with source art, import metadata, prefab reference, scripts, tests, build config
must_not_conclude: every repository member is creative or binary is current; path is not a fact

observations: camera-original metadata and capture naming; no source, import record, or review annotation; clip depicts game screen
must_not_conclude: game-art activation or authored render from depicted content

collides_with.signal: Both contain models, rigs, textures, scenes; game-art requires engine-facing export/import/integration, generic 3D owns modelling/rendering without it.
Both contain animation, VFX, renders and proofs; game-art has asset IDs/prefabs/scenes/import settings, motion has storyboard/composition/render delivery.
Both contain video proofs/effects; recorded source and editorial timeline belong to post-production, engine capture belongs here only with asset linkage.
Both contain engine projects, JSON, shaders and binaries; code owns repository/scripts/tests/build tooling, this role owns visual/audio production handoff.
Both contain PNG/JPG/screens; EXIF/capture evidence belongs to photos, generated atlas/texture/review image needs production linkage.

also_holds_with.signal: Layered sprite, UI, icon and visual-development work may be both design and game-asset production when engine handoff is evidenced.
Licensed marketplace asset may enter an engine packet; rights/provenance remain distinct.

falls_through_to.why: Detached concept art, texture, icon, or screenshot is isolated.
Gameplay/tutorial/reference video without authored packet is a clip.
Ambiguous binary, detached export, cache, or incomplete packet needs human review.
Standalone manifest, note, or build report remains a record.
Unreadable packages retain metadata until approved extraction or user attachment.

role_split.this_role: authored game art, import metadata, asset IDs, and visual/audio evidence
role_split.neighbour_role: scripts, repository structure, tests, build tooling, runtime code

sensitivity_why: Unreleased characters, levels, mechanics, proprietary assets, licensed packages, build manifests and review captures can expose confidential development or third-party rights; posture follows packet and rights, not extension.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: Should a later creative field pass license project, lifecycle_stage, asset_type, and engine_target, or keep this structural until integration metadata is consistently extractable? NEEDS-JOSEPH: When packets include source footage or soundtrack, should co-holding remain permitted or should role split be stricter?
